requirement: Limit system access to authorized users, processes acting on behalf of authorized users, and devices (including other systems).
implementation_statement: Enclave accounts are created in SYS-01 after U.S.-person verification and manager approval (318 accounts). Plant 2 MES uses shared terminal logins. Access reviews are semiannual. Sample: 2 of 25 terminations had enclave access removed 3 and 6 days late. Planned: Plant 2 MES sign-in through SYS-01 named accounts; HR-triggered same-day disable; quarterly reviews (target 2027-01-31).
evidence: IdP export 2026-07-14; sample of 25 of 96 terminations; Plant 2 MES user table; review record 2026-02-27

requirement: Limit system access to the types of transactions and functions that authorized users are permitted to execute.
implementation_statement: PLM roles limit users to the projects and lifecycle functions their job requires; MES roles at Plant 1 separate operator, lead, and programmer functions.
evidence: PLM role matrix; Plant 1 MES role table; sample of 25 PLM users

requirement: Control the flow of CUI in accordance with approved authorizations.
implementation_statement: MFT partner folders are separated and suite sharing is limited to 31 allow-listed domains. The AI-003 predictive maintenance gateway sends CNC telemetry, including active program names, from the Plant 1 shop-floor VLAN to a vendor commercial cloud; this flow is not authorized in the SSP. Planned: Move the gateway to an OT DMZ; strip program names; document approved CUI flows in SSP section 8 (target 2026-11-30).
evidence: MFT folder permissions; sharing policy; gateway traffic capture 2026-07-22

requirement: Separate the duties of individuals to reduce the risk of malevolent activity without collusion.
implementation_statement: Duties are separated: log and SIEM administration sits with the security team, backup administration with 2 named backup administrators, and cloud administration with the infrastructure team.
evidence: Role assignment export; RACI in POL-02

requirement: Employ the principle of least privilege, including for specific security functions and privileged accounts.
implementation_statement: Enclave users are standard users and administrators use just-in-time elevation. At Plant 2, MES terminals run under an administrator account and operators can edit NC programs. Planned: Standard-user terminals; program-edit rights limited to NC programmers (target 2027-01-31).
evidence: Local-group report; Plant 2 terminal configuration; walkthrough 2026-08-12

requirement: Use non-privileged accounts or roles when accessing nonsecurity functions
implementation_statement: Administrators use separate privileged accounts activated just in time with hardware security keys; standard accounts for email and browsing.
evidence: Privileged role assignments; sample of all 12 administrators

requirement: Prevent non-privileged users from executing privileged functions and capture the execution of such functions in audit logs.
implementation_statement: Privileged role activation and administrator actions are logged in SYS-01 and the cloud audit log and sent to the SIEM; Plant 1 MES logs program edits by named user.
evidence: SIEM sample of privileged activations; MES audit table

requirement: Limit unsuccessful logon attempts.
implementation_statement: SYS-01 locks accounts after 10 failed attempts; Plant 1 MES uses SYS-01; the Plant 2 MES local lockout setting is enabled (5 attempts).
evidence: IdP lockout policy; Plant 2 MES security settings

requirement: Provide privacy and security notices consistent with applicable CUI rules.
implementation_statement: A logon banner with CUI and monitoring notice displays on enclave endpoints, virtual desktops, and MES terminals at both plants.

requirement: Use session lock with pattern-hiding displays to prevent access and viewing of data after a period of inactivity
implementation_statement: Enclave endpoints and Plant 1 terminals lock after 15 minutes with a pattern-hiding screen. Plant 2 terminals never lock because the shared login stays open all shift. Planned: Resolved with named sign-in and badge tap-out at Plant 2 terminals (target 2027-01-31).

requirement: Terminate (automatically) a user session after a defined condition.
implementation_statement: Suite and virtual desktop sessions end after 30 minutes idle and 12 hours total; MES web sessions end at shift change.

requirement: Monitor and control remote access sessions.
implementation_statement: Remote access to the enclave is only through the virtual desktop gateway with MFA and device compliance; sessions are logged and monitored by the MSSP.
evidence: Conditional access policies; SIEM remote access report

requirement: Employ cryptographic mechanisms to protect the confidentiality of remote access sessions.
implementation_statement: Gateway sessions use TLS through the provider's FIPS-validated modules (CRM).

requirement: Route remote access via managed access control points.
implementation_statement: All remote access is routed through the provider-managed gateway in the shared services account; no other inbound path exists.
evidence: Network security group rules; external scan 2026-07-20

requirement: Authorize remote execution of privileged commands and remote access to security-relevant information.
implementation_statement: Remote privileged commands require just-in-time activation through the privileged access broker.

requirement: Authorize wireless access prior to allowing such connections
implementation_statement: Wireless networks are authorized by the IT Director; no wireless on enclave VLANs at Plant 1.

requirement: Protect wireless access using authentication and encryption
implementation_statement: Corporate Wi-Fi uses enterprise authentication. At Plant 2, handheld scanners use a shared-key network on the flat network that also reaches shop-floor systems. Planned: Move scanners to enterprise authentication on an isolated VLAN (target 2026-12-31).
evidence: Wireless configuration export; Plant 2 network walk 2026-08-12

requirement: Control connection of mobile devices.
implementation_statement: Mobile phones reach enclave services only through the managed authenticator and suite apps with app protection; unmanaged devices are blocked.

requirement: Encrypt CUI on mobile devices and mobile computing platforms.[23]
implementation_statement: Enclave laptops use full-disk encryption with FIPS-validated modules; phones use app-level protection.

requirement: Verify and control/limit connections to and use of external systems.
implementation_statement: Personal devices and public file-sharing are blocked from the enclave. The AI-003 gateway connects the Plant 1 shop-floor VLAN to an external vendor cloud, and the AI-001 pilot was enabled before the provider confirmed it is inside the authorized boundary. Planned: Move the gateway out of the enclave; obtain boundary confirmation for AI-001 or disable it (target 2026-10-31).
evidence: Gateway traffic capture; AI-001 enablement record 2026-05-11

requirement: Limit use of portable storage devices on external systems.
implementation_statement: Removable media is blocked on enclave endpoints by device control, except the inventoried USB drives used at legacy CNC machines (see 3.8.7).

requirement: Control CUI posted or processed on publicly accessible systems.
responsible_role: Director of Trade Compliance and Contracts
implementation_statement: Public website content and trade show material are reviewed and released by the Director of Trade Compliance and Contracts.

requirement: Ensure that managers, systems administrators, and users of organizational systems are made aware of the security risks associated with their activities and of the applicable policies, standards, and procedures related to the security of those systems.
implementation_statement: Annual security awareness and CUI handling training for all workforce members, including Plant 2 staff since 2025; 97% completion; phishing simulations quarterly.
evidence: Training records 2026-06-30; simulation results (6.1% click rate)

requirement: Ensure that personnel are trained to carry out their assigned information security-related duties and responsibilities.
implementation_statement: Role-based training for administrators, engineers who mark CUI, quality staff who distribute drawings, and manufacturing systems staff, delivered annually.
evidence: Role curriculum; completion records for 4 roles

requirement: Provide security awareness training on recognizing and reporting potential indicators of insider threat.
implementation_statement: Annual training does not cover insider threat indicators or how to report them. Planned: Insider threat module with reporting channel in the annual training (target 2026-12-31).

requirement: Create and retain system audit logs and records to the extent needed to enable the monitoring, analysis, investigation, and reporting of unlawful or unauthorized system activity
implementation_statement: Cloud, identity, suite, endpoint, and Plant 1 firewall logs reach the SIEM with 1-year retention. MES, DNC, OT, and all Plant 2 network logs are not collected. Planned: Onboard MES, DNC, OT gateway, and Plant 2 firewall logs to the SIEM (target 2027-01-31).
evidence: SIEM data source list; MSSP statement of work

requirement: Ensure that the actions of individual system users can be uniquely traced to those users, so they can be held accountable for their actions.
implementation_statement: Cloud and Plant 1 MES actions trace to named users. Plant 2 MES actions show only the shared login. Planned: Resolved by named Plant 2 MES accounts (3.5.1) (target 2027-01-31).

requirement: Review and update logged events.
implementation_statement: Logged event types are reviewed each year by the security team with the MSSP; last review 2026-03.

requirement: Alert in the event of an audit logging process failure.
implementation_statement: The SIEM alerts the MSSP when a log source stops sending for more than 1 hour.

requirement: Correlate audit record review, analysis, and reporting processes for investigation and response to indications of unlawful, unauthorized, suspicious, or unusual activity.
implementation_statement: The MSSP correlates cloud, identity, and endpoint events 24x7. There is no correlation or review for shop-floor or Plant 2 activity. Planned: Add shop-floor use cases after onboarding (3.3.1) (target 2027-01-31).
evidence: MSSP monthly report; use case list

requirement: Provide audit record reduction and report generation to support on-demand analysis and reporting.
implementation_statement: The SIEM provides query, reduction, and reporting; saved reports exist for investigations.

requirement: Provide a system capability that compares and synchronizes internal system clocks with an authoritative source to generate time stamps for audit records
implementation_statement: Enclave systems, MES, DNC, and OT controllers that support it synchronize to an authoritative time source.
evidence: Time configuration check on 10 sampled systems

requirement: Protect audit information and audit logging tools from unauthorized access, modification, and deletion.
implementation_statement: Logs are stored in the SIEM and a write-once archive; access is limited to the security team and the MSSP.
evidence: SIEM access list; archive retention lock

requirement: Limit management of audit logging functionality to a subset of privileged users.
implementation_statement: Only the Security Manager and one analyst can change log settings; infrastructure administrators cannot.

requirement: Establish and maintain baseline configurations and inventories of organizational systems (including hardware, software, firmware, and documentation) throughout the respective system development life cycles.
implementation_statement: Baselines and inventory exist for cloud workloads and endpoints. No documented baselines for MES, DNC, or OT servers at either plant; the Plant 2 OT inventory is a 2024 spreadsheet. Planned: Baselines and inventory for MES, DNC, and OT servers at both plants (target 2027-01-31).
evidence: Baseline library; asset inventory; OT spreadsheet

requirement: Establish and enforce security configuration settings for information technology products employed in organizational systems.
implementation_statement: Benchmark settings are enforced on cloud workloads and endpoints. MES and DNC servers are not hardened. Planned: Harden MES and DNC servers to the baseline; Plant 2 servers replaced (3.14.1) (target 2027-01-31).
evidence: Configuration scan of 10 cloud servers; MES server review

requirement: Track, review, approve or disapprove, and log changes to organizational systems.
implementation_statement: Cloud and endpoint changes go through the change advisory board with tickets. Shop-floor server and network changes are informal at both plants. Planned: Bring MES, DNC, and OT network changes into the change process (target 2026-12-31).
evidence: Change tickets (sample of 20); interview Manufacturing Systems Manager

requirement: Analyze the security impact of changes prior to implementation.
implementation_statement: Change tickets for enclave systems include a security impact analysis reviewed by the security team.

requirement: Define, document, approve, and enforce physical and logical access restrictions associated with changes to organizational systems.
implementation_statement: Change rights in the cloud and at Plant 1 are limited to named administrators. At Plant 2 any operator can edit programs through the shared MES login. Planned: Program-edit rights limited to NC programmers through named accounts (target 2027-01-31).

requirement: Employ the principle of least functionality by configuring organizational systems to provide only essential capabilities.
implementation_statement: Enclave images include only approved functions; unused services are removed from cloud workloads.

requirement: Restrict, disable, or prevent the use of nonessential programs, functions, ports, protocols, and services.
implementation_statement: Cloud and Plant 1 rules allow only documented ports. The Plant 2 legacy MES server exposes remote desktop and an outdated file-sharing protocol to the whole plant network. Planned: Close remote desktop and legacy file sharing; restrict by the OT DMZ design (target 2026-11-30).

requirement: Apply deny-by-exception (blacklisting) policy to prevent the use of unauthorized software or deny-all, permit-by-exception (whitelisting) policy to allow the execution of authorized software.
implementation_statement: Application allowlisting is enforced on CAD workstations and Plant 1 terminals. Plant 2 terminals and servers have no allowlisting. Planned: Extend allowlisting to Plant 2 terminals and replacement servers (target 2027-01-31).

requirement: Control and monitor user-installed software.
implementation_statement: Users cannot install software on enclave endpoints; installations go through device management.

requirement: Identify system users, processes acting on behalf of users, and devices.
implementation_statement: Users, service accounts, and devices are identified in SYS-01 and device management. Plant 2 MES terminals use shared logins. Planned: Named accounts with badge plus PIN at Plant 2 terminals, as at Plant 1 (target 2027-01-31).
evidence: IdP export; Plant 2 MES user table

requirement: Authenticate (or verify) the identities of users, processes, or devices, as a prerequisite to allowing access to organizational systems.
implementation_statement: SYS-01 authenticates every enclave user and device before access. Plant 2 MES does not authenticate individuals. Planned: Same as 3.5.1 (target 2027-01-31).

requirement: Use multifactor authentication for local and network access to privileged accounts and for network access to non-privileged accounts.[24] [25].
implementation_statement: MFA is enforced for all network access to enclave services and for administrators (hardware keys). Local administrator access to MES and DNC servers at both plants uses passwords only, and Plant 2 terminals have no MFA. Planned: MFA for server administration through the access broker; Plant 2 terminals on badge plus PIN (target 2027-01-31).
evidence: Conditional access policy; MES server local admin review

requirement: Employ replay-resistant authentication mechanisms for network access to privileged and non-privileged accounts.
implementation_statement: Enclave authentication uses replay-resistant protocols through SYS-01.

requirement: Prevent reuse of identifiers for a defined period.
implementation_statement: Identifiers are never reused; the IdP keeps disabled identifiers.

requirement: Disable identifiers after a defined period of inactivity.
implementation_statement: Accounts inactive for 45 days are disabled automatically, with a monthly report.

requirement: Enforce a minimum password complexity and change of characters when new passwords are created.
implementation_statement: Passwords must be at least 14 characters and are checked against a banned list in SYS-01.

requirement: Prohibit password reuse for a specified number of generations.
implementation_statement: SYS-01 prevents reuse of the last 24 passwords.

requirement: Allow temporary password use for system logons with an immediate change to a permanent password.
implementation_statement: Temporary passwords require change at first sign-in.

requirement: Store and transmit only cryptographically-protected passwords.
implementation_statement: SYS-01 stores only protected credentials. The Plant 2 DNC service credential is stored in plain text in a configuration file. Planned: Move the credential to the vault; rotate it (target 2026-10-31).

requirement: Obscure feedback of authentication information
implementation_statement: Authentication feedback is obscured on all enclave sign-in screens and terminals.

requirement: Establish an operational incident-handling capability for organizational systems that includes preparation, detection, analysis, containment, recovery, and user response activities.
implementation_statement: POL-03 and the incident response plan set preparation, detection, analysis, containment, recovery, and user response; the MSSP provides 24x7 detection and a forensic firm is on retainer through the insurer panel.
evidence: Incident response plan; MSSP contract; retainer letter

requirement: Track, document, and report incidents to designated officials and/or authorities both internal and external to the organization.
responsible_role: Director of Trade Compliance and Contracts
implementation_statement: Incidents are tracked in the ticket system and two medium assurance certificates are held. No DIBNet drill since 2024, Plant 2 and OT events are not tracked through the SIEM, and the image preservation procedure covers cloud systems only. Planned: DIBNet drill in the 2026-11-18 tabletop; OT and MES imaging procedure (target 2026-11-30).
evidence: Incident log (14 incidents in 12 months); certificate records

requirement: Test the organizational incident response capability.
implementation_statement: A ransomware tabletop was held in 2025-09. No exercise has covered CUI exfiltration or the DoD reporting steps. Planned: CUI exfiltration tabletop with DIBNet drill (2026-11-18) (target 2026-11-30).

requirement: Perform maintenance on organizational systems.[26].
implementation_statement: Maintenance on enclave and shop-floor systems is scheduled and recorded in the maintenance system.

requirement: Provide controls on the tools, techniques, mechanisms, and personnel used to conduct system maintenance.
implementation_statement: Maintenance tools are approved and controlled by the manufacturing systems team and IT.

requirement: Ensure equipment removed for off-site maintenance is sanitized of any CUI.
implementation_statement: Equipment leaving for repair has storage removed or sanitized first; certificates kept.

requirement: Check media containing diagnostic and test programs for malicious code before the media are used in organizational systems.
implementation_statement: Vendor diagnostic laptops and media brought to CNC machines, additive printers, and test stands are not scanned before use at either plant. Planned: Scanning kiosk at both plants; vendor media rule in the maintenance procedure (target 2026-12-31).
evidence: Interviews with both plant maintenance leads; walkthrough

requirement: Require multifactor authentication to establish nonlocal maintenance sessions via external network connections and terminate such connections when nonlocal maintenance is complete.
implementation_statement: Machine tool vendors connect through the company access broker with MFA and session recording. The additive printer vendor connects through its own remote support tool with no company MFA or recording. Planned: Move additive printer vendor access to the broker; block the vendor tool (target 2026-10-31).
evidence: Broker session logs; additive printer remote tool review

requirement: Supervise the maintenance activities of maintenance personnel without required access authorization.
implementation_statement: Vendor technicians without enclave access are escorted while on site.

requirement: Protect (i.e., physically control and securely store) system media containing CUI, both paper and digital.
implementation_statement: Plant 1 keeps printed drawings in cell cabinets and returns them to quality at job close. Plant 2 keeps printed drawings in open racks. Planned: Lockable cell cabinets and the job-close return rule at Plant 2 (target 2026-11-30).
evidence: Walkthrough of 8 cells at both plants

requirement: Limit access to CUI on system media to authorized users
implementation_statement: Access to CUI on media is limited to enclave users; printing requires sign-in at the printer (secure print release).

requirement: Sanitize or destroy system media containing CUI before disposal or release for reuse.
implementation_statement: Plant 1 uses locked shred bins with a destruction vendor. At Plant 2, printed drawings were found in general recycling in 3 of 5 cells. Planned: Locked shred bins at Plant 2 under the same vendor contract (target 2026-10-31).

requirement: Mark media with necessary CUI markings and distribution limitations.[27]
implementation_statement: Plant 1 MES prints a CUI banner on travelers. Plant 2 legacy MES printouts have no CUI marking. Planned: Marking template in the Plant 2 MES until replacement (target 2026-11-30).

requirement: Control access to media containing CUI and maintain accountability for media during transport outside of controlled areas.
implementation_statement: Printed CUI leaves a plant only in sealed envelopes logged by quality, for suppliers with flowdown.

requirement: Implement cryptographic mechanisms to protect the confidentiality of CUI stored on digital media during transport unless otherwise protected by alternative physical safeguards.
implementation_statement: Enclave laptops and the inventoried USB drives use FIPS-validated encryption.
evidence: Encryption report; USB drive model list

requirement: Control the use of removable media on system components.
implementation_statement: Plant 1 machines all load from DNC. At Plant 2, 8 legacy CNC machines are loaded from USB drives that are not inventoried or labeled. Planned: Inventoried labeled drives now; DNC serial gateway for the 8 machines (target 2027-01-31).

requirement: Prohibit the use of portable storage devices when such devices have no identifiable owner.
implementation_statement: Five USB drives with no identifiable owner were found at Plant 2 legacy machines. Planned: Remove unowned drives; issue labeled drives only (target 2026-10-31).

requirement: Protect the confidentiality of backup CUI at storage locations.
implementation_statement: Cloud and Plant 1 backups are encrypted in the backup account. Plant 2 MES and DNC backups sit unencrypted on a local storage device. Planned: Encrypted nightly backups of Plant 2 MES and DNC to the backup account (target 2026-11-30).

requirement: Screen individuals prior to authorizing access to organizational systems containing CUI.
implementation_statement: Background checks and U.S.-person verification are completed before enclave access.

requirement: Ensure that organizational systems containing CUI are protected during and after personnel actions such as terminations and transfers
implementation_statement: HR terminations trigger account disablement. Sample: 2 of 25 terminations had enclave access removed 3 and 6 days late, and shared Plant 2 MES passwords are not changed when operators leave. Planned: Same-day automated disable; named accounts at Plant 2 (target 2027-01-31).
evidence: Sample of 25 of 96 terminations; Plant 2 password history

requirement: Limit physical access to organizational systems, equipment, and the respective operating environments to authorized individuals.
implementation_statement: Badge access controls the engineering center, server rooms, and shop floors at both plants.

requirement: Protect and monitor the physical facility and support infrastructure for organizational systems.
implementation_statement: Cameras and badge logs monitor both plants; the facilities team reviews alarms daily.

requirement: Escort visitors and monitor visitor activity.
implementation_statement: Plant 1 escorts and badges all visitors. At Plant 2, 2 unescorted visitors were seen on the shop floor during the walkthrough. Planned: Visitor management system and escort rule at Plant 2 (target 2026-10-31).

requirement: Maintain audit logs of physical access.
implementation_statement: Plant 1 uses an electronic visitor system. The Plant 2 paper log missed 11 of 38 July visits found in the gate camera review. Planned: Electronic visitor system at Plant 2 (target 2026-10-31).

requirement: Control and manage physical access devices.
implementation_statement: Badges, keys, and lock combinations are inventoried; badge access is reviewed quarterly.

requirement: Enforce safeguarding measures for CUI at alternate work sites.
implementation_statement: Remote work with CUI uses enclave laptops or virtual desktops only; printing CUI at home is prohibited.

requirement: Periodically assess the risk to organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, or reputation), organizational assets, and individuals, resulting from the operation of organizational systems and the associated processing, storage, or transmission of CUI
implementation_statement: Annual risk assessment using NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (this year's register in P01).

requirement: Scan for vulnerabilities in organizational systems and applications periodically and when new vulnerabilities affecting those systems and applications are identified.
implementation_statement: Quarterly authenticated scans cover cloud workloads and endpoints. MES and DNC servers at both plants and all Plant 2 systems are not scanned. Planned: Monthly scans including MES and DNC (passive OT discovery for controllers) (target 2026-12-31).
evidence: Scan schedule; scan reports Q1 and Q2 2026

requirement: Remediate vulnerabilities in accordance with risk assessments.
implementation_statement: Cloud and endpoint findings are remediated within the standard (Critical 15 days, High 30 days). Shop-floor findings are not tracked. Planned: Track shop-floor findings with risk-based compensating controls (target 2026-12-31).

requirement: Periodically assess the security controls in organizational systems to determine if the controls are effective in their application.
implementation_statement: The 2025 self-assessment covered Plant 1 only and accepted policy documents as evidence for some technical requirements. Planned: Full self-assessment against SP 800-171A objectives for both plants (target 2026-12-31).

requirement: Develop and implement plans of action designed to correct deficiencies and reduce or eliminate vulnerabilities in organizational systems.
implementation_statement: A POA&M has been kept since 2025 but does not include Plant 2 or the AI tools. Planned: Rebuild the POA&M from P07 and this analysis; monthly review (target 2026-10-31).

requirement: Monitor security controls on an ongoing basis to ensure the continued effectiveness of the controls.
implementation_statement: The MSSP reports monthly; the Security Manager reports control metrics to the COO monthly and the audit committee quarterly.
evidence: Monthly metric reports; audit committee minutes

requirement: Develop, document, and periodically update system security plans that describe system boundaries, system environments of operation, how security requirements are implemented, and the relationships with or connections to other systems.[28]
implementation_statement: SSP v3.0 (2025-05-30) did not include Plant 2 or the MSSP as an External Service Provider. SSP v4.0 (P02, 2026-09-17) covers both and must be verified. Planned: Verify SSP v4.0 in the readiness re-check; update after each major change (target 2026-10-31).

requirement: Monitor, control, and protect communications (i.e., information transmitted or received by organizational systems) at the external boundaries and key internal boundaries of organizational systems.
implementation_statement: The cloud enclave and Plant 1 are protected by managed boundaries. At Plant 2, the shop floor shares a flat network with the corporate segment. Planned: Separate Plant 2 shop-floor VLANs behind an enclave firewall (target 2027-01-31).

requirement: Employ architectural designs, software development techniques, and systems engineering principles that promote effective information security within organizational systems.
implementation_statement: The landing zone design separates identity, shared services, workloads, and backup accounts, with deny-by-default routing.

requirement: Separate user functionality from system management functionality.
implementation_statement: Administration uses separate privileged accounts and the access broker; user functions are separate from management interfaces.

requirement: Prevent unauthorized and unintended information transfer via shared system resources.
implementation_statement: Shared resources are cleared by the provider (CRM) and by enclave session settings.

requirement: Implement subnetworks for publicly accessible system components that are physically or logically separated from internal networks.
implementation_statement: The MFT gateway and virtual desktop gateway sit in separate subnets in the shared services account.

requirement: Deny network communications traffic by default and allow network communications traffic by exception (i.e., deny all, permit by exception).
implementation_statement: Cloud and Plant 1 boundaries deny by default. Plant 2 has no boundary to apply it to. Planned: Part of the Plant 2 enclave firewall (3.13.1) (target 2027-01-31).

requirement: Prevent remote devices from simultaneously establishing non-remote connections with organizational systems and communicating via some other connection to resources in external networks (i.e., split tunneling).
implementation_statement: Split tunneling is disabled on enclave laptops.

requirement: Implement cryptographic mechanisms to prevent unauthorized disclosure of CUI during transmission unless otherwise protected by alternative physical safeguards.
implementation_statement: CUI in transit is encrypted on all paths (TLS, IPsec, SSH).

requirement: Terminate network connections associated with communications sessions at the end of the sessions or after a defined period of inactivity.
implementation_statement: Network sessions end after inactivity on the gateways and firewalls.

requirement: Establish and manage cryptographic keys for cryptography employed in organizational systems.
implementation_statement: Keys are managed in the key management service with company-controlled keys.

requirement: Employ FIPS-validated cryptography when used to protect the confidentiality of CUI.
implementation_statement: FIPS-validated modules are confirmed for the cloud services (CRM), MFT gateway, site-to-cloud VPN, and endpoints. The Plant 2 SD-WAN appliance encrypts traffic but runs in non-FIPS mode. Planned: Enable FIPS mode or replace the Plant 2 appliance (target 2026-11-30).
evidence: Cryptographic module table in SSP v4.0; appliance configuration

requirement: Prohibit remote activation of collaborative computing devices and provide indication of devices in use to users present at the device.[29].
implementation_statement: Collaborative devices (cameras, microphones) in enclave areas cannot be activated remotely and show an indicator.

requirement: Control and monitor the use of mobile code.
implementation_statement: Mobile code is controlled through browser and script policies on enclave endpoints.

requirement: Control and monitor the use of Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) technologies.
implementation_statement: No VoIP components in the CMMC Assessment Scope (telephones are on the corporate network).

requirement: Protect the authenticity of communications sessions.
implementation_statement: Session authenticity is protected by TLS with certificate validation.

requirement: Protect the confidentiality of CUI at rest.
implementation_statement: CUI at rest is encrypted in the cloud and on endpoints. Plant 2 MES server disks and local backups are not encrypted. Planned: Encrypted replacement servers and backups at Plant 2 (target 2027-01-31).

requirement: Identify, report, and correct system flaws in a timely manner.
implementation_statement: Cloud and endpoint patches follow the standard. The Plant 2 MES and DNC servers run an operating system past end of vendor support; Plant 1 MES servers are 2 quarters behind. Planned: Replace Plant 2 servers; quarterly MES patch windows at Plant 1 (target 2027-01-31).

requirement: Provide protection from malicious code at designated locations within organizational systems.
implementation_statement: EDR protects all enclave endpoints and servers, including the Plant 2 servers on a supported legacy agent.

requirement: Monitor system security alerts and advisories and take action in response.
implementation_statement: The security team and MSSP receive vendor and government advisories and act on them.

requirement: Update malicious code protection mechanisms when new releases are available.
implementation_statement: EDR signatures and engines update automatically.

requirement: Perform periodic scans of organizational systems and real-time scans of files from external sources as files are downloaded, opened, or executed.
implementation_statement: EDR scans continuously and scans files from external sources on access.

requirement: Monitor organizational systems, including inbound and outbound communications traffic, to detect attacks and indicators of potential attacks.
implementation_statement: The MSSP monitors cloud, identity, endpoints, and Plant 1 firewalls for attacks, including egress anomalies. Shop-floor networks at both plants are not monitored. Planned: Passive OT network monitoring at both plants feeding the SIEM (target 2027-01-31).

requirement: Identify unauthorized use of organizational systems.
implementation_statement: Unauthorized use is detected for cloud and identity events. There is no detection for MES, DNC, or OT use. Planned: Shop-floor use cases after onboarding (3.3.1) (target 2027-01-31).
